correctness.rationale: The geometric blow-up classes explicitly generate the 16x10 binary incidence: four reducible fibers and eight distinct line components per pencil. Every Frobenius-invariant integral permutation module has its canonical orbit-sum basis; the induced map counts incident members, without dividing by orbit sizes. All 1920 elements of W(D5) are enumerated and partitioned into exactly eighteen proved conjugacy classes. An exact unimodular integer Smith algorithm checks every orbit matrix and a second independent SymPy Smith algorithm agrees on eighteen representatives. The five-cycle 4x2 matrix gives gcd entries 1 and gcd maximal minors 10, so its cokernel is Z^2 plus Z/10. The theorem does not claim sampled finite-field data as proof.

originality.rationale: A precise new domain is the Frobenius-invariant integral morphism from orbit sums of the ten conic-fibration labels to orbit sums of the sixteen exceptional-line labels. The principal literature gives ten fibrations, Weyl representations, finite-field trace types or different Picard/graph lattices, but the inspected primary sections and closest complete published results do not imply the Z/10 obstruction or eighteen exact cokernels. Searches and claim-level comparisons were carried out. Older unindexed D5 integer-incidence tables remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: An older or unindexed integer-design/signed-permutation incidence Smith table might contain equivalent invariant factors.
Not every of the 18 Weyl classes needs to be realizable over every finite field; theorem is explicitly conditional and does not need universality of realization.
No independent specialist originality assessment has been performed.

value.rationale: The ten conic fibrations and sixteen exceptional curves are canonical geometric configurations. Frobenius-invariant orbit sums of their incidence supports are a natural arithmetic integral reconstruction question. The complete 18-type classification distinguishes torsion-free, 2-torsion and five-primary arithmetic failures invisible over the algebraic closure, with exact free ranks and complete Smith factors. This is a motivated structural classification, not an arbitrary isolated modulus or routine rational-rank computation.
